title: originate verify: scopeTenantFields leaves certification.certifierOrganizationId on the existing cross-tenant answers (v1 /verify, v1 verify-file, v2), against Kam's KS-590 card ruling a
description:
**BLUF:** In originate at develop `07a2d62be6a0`, `scopeTenantFields` nulls `title`, `issuer` and `certification.certifiedBy` on a cross-tenant verify answer but leaves `certification.certifierOrganizationId`. Kam's card `secuura-ks590-verify-disclosure-four-questions-1102` was ruled option a on 2026-11-02 (ruled_ts 12:44:16 +11:00): "Strict: no tenant-owned naming incl. org UUID on all four paths (changes live verify)". PR 2004 (merged as `07a2d62be6a0`) applies that on its NEW path only (D-B3). The EXISTING cross-tenant answers of v1 `/verify`, v1 `verify-file` and v2 still carry the id.

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate192-ks1986-pr2004/ready_2004.txt, FILING CANDIDATES (b) (Seat F 32nd's, lines as of head `577f668f4786`); /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate192-ks1986-pr2004/verdict.md, finding G192-F3 (lines 38 to 44) and the D-B3 lines 74 and 76; the card, read with the `show` verb of /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/2_Project_Files/tools/decision_queue.sh on 2026-11-05.

## Where (read at develop `07a2d62be6a0`)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts`, `scopeTenantFields` lines 463 to 474: `title` and `issuer` become null and `certification.certifiedBy` becomes null; no other certification key changes.
* `buildCertification` (lines 164 to 175) sets `certifierOrganizationId: certMeta.issuerId ?? null` (line 173). The chain-derived certification sets `chain.metadata?.issuerOrgId ?? null` (same file, lines 997 and 1561; `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts` line 237).
* Scope sites on the existing answers: `verify-file` lines 1050 to 1051 (`isCrossTenantResponse`, then `scopeTenantFields`); `/verify` line 1342 (the by-id branch, which adds `certification: buildCertification(doc)`) and lines 1604 to 1606 (the hash path, `scopeTenantFields(buildResponse(...), scoped)`); v2 `buildMatch` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts` lines 194 to 195 (`scopeTenantFields(match, true)` plus `fieldsWithheld: true`).
* The NEW path nulls the id: `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts` lines 584, 658 and 694 (D-B3; the comment at line 584 cites the card).

## What others measured

* Gate 192 on PostgreSQL 15, as reported in KS-1991: v2 at develop and at PR 2004 presents another tenant's certification (`cert-y-1`) with `certifierOrganizationId dddddddd-0000-4000-8000-00000000000d`.
* Gates 192 and 193: every row on the new D-B2 path has `certifierOrganizationId null` and `certifiedBy null`.
* KS-1561, item 5 (Seat J 5th, 2026-10-12, real routes): on the legacy certify path the field carries the issuer's USER id (`certMeta.issuerId = issuer.id`), not an organisation id.
* v1 existing answers (`/verify`, `verify-file`) with a certification present: read from code only; no gate drove them.

## Card detail and scope

The card's option a detail says an agent builds it, that it covers all four of the card's gaps, and: "Verifiers incl. Platform S stop seeing the org id; confirm with Stuart first." This filing does not contact Stuart and assigns nothing to him. The `show` output carries no delivered artefact for the card; whether the ruling reached an artefact is not measured. This ticket covers the card's first point only. The other three (both chain-first branches skip `scopeTenantFields`; rows with no tenancy info are never scrubbed; the by-id path selects no `tenant_id`) were not re-read by this seat.

KS-590 (Peter's ticket, untouched, no comment here) carries the same org-UUID question as the first of its four disclosure questions, in its comments of 2026-08-11 and 2026-10-06.

One test pass: bytes whose certification belongs to another tenant, driven through v1 `/verify`, v1 `verify-file` and v2, reading whether `certification.certifierOrganizationId` is present.

## Grade

Medium, this seat's judgement: an identifier is disclosed on public verify routes against a ruling of Kam's. This seat does not decide the card.

## Not measured

* Any v1 existing answer with a certification present (code read only).
* How many certifications carry an `issuerId`, and what Platform S does with the field, in any environment.
* This seat ran no test and no service; the code facts are reads of a depth-1 clone at `07a2d62be6a0`.

## Related

* KS-590 (Peter's, above); KS-1561 (item 5); KS-1986 (PR 2004's ticket); KS-1991 (G192-F1).
* Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, archived included): `scopeTenantFields` 1 open (KS-590), 0 closed; `isCrossTenantResponse` 1 open (KS-590), 0 closed; `tenant-owned naming` 1 open (KS-590), 0 closed; `org UUID` 2 open (KS-590, KS-1986), 0 closed; `certifierOrganizationId` 5 open (KS-590, KS-735, KS-772, KS-1561, KS-1991), 1 closed (KS-1557). Control: `platform_document_registry` 16 open, 9 closed. KS-590 was read whole; KS-1561 item 5 and KS-1991 were read; KS-735 and KS-772 appear in the hits and this seat read their titles only. No open ticket other than KS-590 names the id's survival through `scopeTenantFields`, and KS-590 is a test-coverage ticket that asks Kam the question.

nodes.body:
**Live evidence from Platform S for this class, Kintsugi, 10 Nov 2026 (S ticket PS-1650).** Two S organisations registered the same bytes (`ec5d82c1…`):
* Obeden PTE Ltd first, on 9 Nov, as K document `e0d2da10-…`;
* ISS Three second, on 10 Nov, as `90101413-…`, and then declared it.

When ISS Three verified the file, K's answer to `POST /api/verification/verify` named the original registrant. S showed ISS Three the issuer "Obeden PTE Ltd", K reference `e0d2da10-…`, and transaction `4ec68662…`, which is another tenant's issuer name and identifiers.

S will fix its own side (PS-1650): pass the viewer's own document as the preferred document when the viewer's organisation holds the bytes. That leaves the anonymous case, and the case of a viewer whose organisation holds no copy, as K's to rule on: should a cross-tenant answer carry the original registrant's issuer name at all?
